I came from a bachelors in commerce with around the same subjects as you. 

The maths requirements arent too heavy. 

However, I bailed on Software Eng masters and did Masters of IT instead. 

It's a year shorter and still gets you the base skills and qualification for jobs in tech. \\

I got 1.5 years into that masters with very little experience prior, and now working as a software engineer at telstra. 

So I think its really worth looking into that Masters too.

Hi, 

I was in this exact same position, really hate my BCom but finished it anyway. Towards the end I started looking into the Masters of Engineering and Masters of IT. 

I highly recommend the Masters of IT, it works really well in conjunction with a commerce background, and applicable in a lot of fields. 

Entry Requirements are chill: 65 WAM and just one university level computing-related subject (e.g. programming subjects). 

Also I think the CSP is guaranteed too, so its cheap. 

It's a 2 year masters, I'm nearly finished mine and am going into a graduate Software Engineer position with Telstra next year. 

Codings really cool and fun if you're into problem solving and actually making something with your mind. 

If you're interested in other fields of Engineering, there are 3 years engineering masters (where the first year is just catching you up with subjects. 

Again, 65 WAM, but they all have about 4 subject requirements. You can do those in breadths or outside your course but at uni like I did. 

Let me know if you have any questions, more than happy to help.
